item.title: Chips Drag Emerging Stocks to April Low, Oil Shields Currencies
item.description: The slide in the Asian tech stocks pushed the benchmark for emerging markets to the lowest in three months, though the pullback in oil prices helped shield European bourses and currencies from the selloff.

item.title: Indian Tax Crackdown Threatens to Slow Exports of Low-Grade Ore
item.description: India’s top iron ore-producing state is increasing quality-control checks after some miners were found to be misrepresenting grades in order to pay lower royalties, according to a document seen by Bloomberg, a crackdown that could hit domestic and export sales.

item.title: StanChart Sees Exit of Several Top Wealth Executives in India
item.description: Standard Chartered Plc. has seen several senior executive departures from its Indian operations as the lender reorganizes its wealth business and shifts away from mass-market retail banking.

item.title: US Publishes Photo Showing Rare Joint Coast Guard Sailing With Taiwan Vessel
item.description: The de facto US embassy in Taiwan has published a photo of US and Taiwanese coast guard vessels sailing together, a rare move that appears aimed at reassuring Taipei as China steps up pressure in the region.

item.title: UAE: Dubai’s Financial Hub DIFC Tops 10,000 Firms Despite War Risks
item.description: Dubai’s financial hub topped 10,000 active registered companies for the first time, underscoring the emirate’s continued success in attracting global firms despite a period of heightened geopolitical tensions in the region.

item.title: Traders Stick With Europe’s Big Rate Curve Bet After Painful Run
item.description: Traders are holding onto one of Europe’s most popular interest-rate bets, even though it’s been pushed off course time and again this year.

item.title: US Tech Stocks Poised to Slide as Global Chip Selloff Deepens
item.description: US technology stocks were set to slump, tracking a rout in global semiconductor shares as concerns over artificial intelligence spending were compounded by rising competition from China.

item.title: Unite Eyes Sale of 20,000 Beds in Pivot to Top Universities
item.description: Unite Group Plc is planning to sell as many as 20,000 student dorms as the landlord reshapes its portfolio to focus on the UK’s top universities as the country’s wider higher education market contends with a series of challenges.

item.title: French Consumer Confidence Increases to Highest Since March
item.description: French consumer confidence advanced more than expected in July, recovering some lost ground since the start of the Iran war.

item.title: Man Group Assets Hit All Time High After Bumper First Half
item.description: Man Group Plc hit a 16 year high after the company’s assets jumped to a record in the first half of the year as clients poured money into the firm’s long-only investment strategies and strong performance gains helped drive growth.

item.title: Tankers Divert to Egypt as Houthi Threat Upends Red Sea Trade
item.description: Empty supertankers are heading to Egypt’s Mediterranean port of Sidi Kerir to collect Saudi crude as observable traffic at the kingdom’s key Red Sea export hub dwindles following threats from Houthi militants.

item.title: Unilever Lifts Outlook as Emerging Markets Drive Dove and Rexona Sales Growth
item.description: Unilever Plc lifted its outlook after sales rose more than expected in the second quarter, as consumers in key markets including the US and India snapped up its Dove soap.

item.title: Taiwan Five-Year Yield Jumps to Highest Since 2008 on Rate Bets
item.description: Taiwan’s five‑year bond yield climbed to the highest level in almost two decades as a disappointing 20-year sale last week and growing expectations for a central bank interest-rate hike sapped demand for the securities.

item.title: Orange Raises Full-Year Estimates on Spain Deal, Africa Growth
item.description: Orange SA raised its profit outlook for the year, driven by growth in the French mobile carrier’s Africa and Middle East markets and the acquisition of a new business in Spain.

item.title: Software Stocks in India Set to Beat Global Chipmakers by Record
item.description: India’s software stocks are set for their biggest monthly outperformance over global chipmakers, signaling investors are moving out of the artificial intelligence trade and into beaten-down information technology names.

item.title: Nvidia Employee Detained by Taiwan in China Chip Smuggling Probe
item.description: Taiwanese prosecutors have detained an Nvidia Corp. employee and searched the company’s offices as part of a widening probe into the alleged smuggling of AI accelerators into China, according to people familiar with the matter.

item.title: Korean Markets Hit by Turmoil as Chip Rout Forces Trading Halts
item.description: South Korean stocks suffered a series of trading suspension on Tuesday, as a selloff in chipmakers spread across sectors.

item.title: AI Boom Propels Hong Kong Exports to Strongest Growth Since 1984
item.description: Hong Kong’s exports surged by the most in more than four decades to hit a record in June, fueled by strong demand from the global boom in artificial intelligence.

item.title: AI to Help UK Recover From Data Crisis, Says Senior Statistician
item.description: Britain’s embattled statistics bureau is hoping artificial intelligence will help alleviate an upcoming budget crunch caused by delays to the launch of a new labor market survey.

item.title: Tokyo Eyes Lifting Support for Overseas Oil Pipeline Investments
item.description: Tokyo is planning to expand its financial support to Japanese companies investing in pipeline projects overseas including the Middle East, as part of efforts to strengthen alternative oil and gas transportation routes in the Gulf region to bypass the Strait of Hormuz.

item.title: Asian Stocks Slide 10% From June Peak to Head for Correction
item.description: Asian stocks slumped, putting the regional benchmark on course for a technical correction, as a selloff in chipmakers deepened.

item.title: RBA’s Bullock Says Economy Cooling, Unsure Rates High Enough
item.description: Australia’s central bank chief said there are signs the economy is cooling as anticipated, though it’s still unclear if this year’s interest-rate hikes are enough to return inflation to target or whether additional tightening will be needed.

item.title: USD/PHP: Philippines Intervened in Small Way to Defend Peso, BSP Governor Says
item.description: The Philippine central bank intervened in a small way to defend the peso last week, Governor Eli Remolona said, as the currency weakened to a record low.

item.title: Bank Indonesia Chief’s Shock Exit Fuels Prabowo Policy Worries
item.description: As recently as Friday, Bank Indonesia Governor Perry Warjiyo was meeting investors in Singapore after a regional central bank forum.

item.title: Malaysia Economy Set to Hit Upper End of Growth Target, BNM Says
item.description: Malaysia’s economy is poised to grow at the upper end of the 4%-5% official forecast for this year, according to the central bank chief.

item.title: India IPO Hopefuls Race to Beat August Deadline for Audited Results
item.description: Three offerings closed on Monday, while four more firms have announced IPO schedules.

item.title: Origin Says About 900,000 Customers’ Data Accessed in Breach
item.description: About 900,000 current and former Origin Energy Ltd. customers had their data accessed in a security breach, the latest in a string of cyberattacks on major Australian companies and essential-service providers.

item.title: Innolight Prices $6.8 Billion Hong Kong Listing Below Maximum
item.description: Zhongji Innolight Co. raised HK$53.4 billion ($6.8 billion) after pricing its Hong Kong listing below the maximum offered in one of the city’s biggest first-time share sale in seven years.

item.title: Anthropic’s Amodei Rejects Open Model Ban But Calls for Testing
item.description: Silicon Valley leaders, including Anthropic PBC Chief Executive Officer Dario Amodei and Nvidia Corp. CEO Jensen Huang, are warning against a broad government crackdown on open-weight artificial intelligence systems as a response to a breakthrough Chinese AI model that’s challenged US leadership in the technology.

item.title: Koei Tecmo Shares Fall as Earnings Miss, Long-Term Doubts Grow
item.description: Shares of Koei Tecmo Holdings Co. fell the most since March after the video-game publisher reported first-quarter operating profit that missed market expectations, underscoring weak software sales and fueling investor concerns about its long-term growth prospects.
